==Problem==

Homer began peeling a pile of 44 potatoes at the rate of 3 potatoes per minute. Four minutes later Christen joined him and peeled at the rate of 5 potatoes per minute. When they finished, how many potatoes had Christen peeled?

<math>\text{(A)}\ 20 \qquad \text{(B)}\ 24 \qquad \text{(C)}\ 32 \qquad \text{(D)}\ 33 \qquad \text{(E)}\ 40</math>

==Solution==

After the <imath> 4 </imath> minutes of Homer peeling alone, he had peeled <imath> 4\times3=12 </imath> potatoes. This means that there are <imath> 44-12=32 </imath> potatoes left. Once Christen joins him, the two are peeling potatoes at a rate of <imath> 3+5=8 </imath> potatoes per minute. So, they finish peeling after another <imath> \frac{32}{8}=4 </imath> minutes. In these <imath> 4 </imath> minutes, Christen peeled <imath> 4\times5=\boxed{\text{A}}  </imath>20 potatoes.

==Solution 2==
After the <imath> 4 </imath> minutes of Homer peeling alone, he had peeled <imath> 4\times3=12 </imath> potatoes. This means that there are <imath> 44-12=32 </imath> potatoes left. Once Christen joins him, the two are peeling potatoes at a rate of <imath> 3+5=8 </imath> potatoes per minute. Because Christen's rate is <imath> 5 </imath>, she peels <imath> 5/8 </imath> of <imath> 32 </imath>, or <imath>20</imath> potatoes.

-N.
